Classification guard: the single edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, mechanismCategory PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL) as a case-matching presentation-and-workup edge on the genitofemoral-nerve-neuralgia, femoral-neuropathy, and levator-ani-syndrome precedent. The neuropathic tongue pain is largely constitutive of the neuralgia, so the edge records that this presentation enters the exclusionary chronic-pain workup rather than asserting a distinct downstream pain disorder. Individual claims require documented lingual neuralgia or lingual nerve injury with neurosensory findings, a dated exclusionary orofacial workup, and review by a qualified medical professional.

Pathway and duplicate-scope screens: no -> trigeminal-neuralgia edge (wrong-identity guard - the Chuang 2026 re-evaluation series lists lingual nerve injury and trigeminal neuralgia as separate final diagnoses in the same differential, and the catalog's trigeminal-neuralgia identity owns the paroxysmal neuralgia pathway with its atypical-odontalgia and auriculotemporal-neuralgia sibling windows); no -> burning-mouth-syndrome edge (the Jaskelainen 2012 review describes subclinical lingual or trigeminal system pathology as one burning-mouth-syndrome subgroup - direction runs from the burning-mouth identity to neuropathic findings, not the reverse, and the burning-mouth identity authors its own windows); no -> depressive-disorder edge (no condition-specific quantified depression cohort located for lingual neuralgia; the neuropathic-pain comorbidity literature is generic to the pain family - reopening condition recorded in governance notes); no -> macroglossia, atrophic-glossitis, or other tongue-site edge (anatomic-site siblings with their own windows; the lingual nerve is sensory to the tongue rather than a tongue-mucosal disease).
governanceNotes: D1 batch 54 (2026-09-25): one bounded association edge authored - lingual-neuralgia to unexplained-chronic-pain (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true; mechanismCategory PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL. The proposition rests on the Chuang 2026 retrospective case series of treatment-refractory non-odontogenic orofacial pain, in which six patients with objective negative dental findings and median 17-month diagnostic delay were re-evaluated under the International Classification of Orofacial Pain, with final diagnoses including persistent idiopathic dentoalveolar pain, lingual nerve injury, trigeminal neuralgia, trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia, and myofascial pain, pain intensity improving from a median numerical rating score of 8 to 0-2 after diagnostic re-evaluation, and documented pitfalls of premature single-cause attribution, overreliance on imaging, and insufficient neurologic examination (PMID 42220291); on the Renton and Yilmaz 2012 management cohort of 216 iatrogenic trigeminal nerve injuries including 93 lingual nerve injuries, in which reassurance and counselling sufficed for 55 percent, systemic or topical medication was offered to 5 percent, cognitive behaviour therapy to 8 percent, topical lidocaine patches reduced pain and allodynia, and exploratory surgery improved symptoms and reduced the neuropathic area in 18 lingual nerve injury patients with improved quality of life (PMID 22326447); and on the Renton 2006 prospective case series of 94 lingual nerve injuries after third molar surgery documenting the limits of conventional sensory assessment and the value of patient-reported subjective function in identifying permanent injury (PMID 16732250). The literature documents a reproducible chronic neuropathic orofacial pain presentation whose exclusionary workup mirrors the unexplained-chronic-pain evaluation without establishing that the neuralgia caused a distinct chronic pain disorder in any individual.

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-25: (i) constitutive-pain guard - the pain defines the neuralgia, so the edge is presentation-and-workup matching rather than a causal arrow, following the genitofemoral-nerve-neuralgia and levator-ani-syndrome precedent; (ii) etiologic scope - the located cohorts are dominated by iatrogenic lingual nerve injury after third molar surgery while the identity name is cause-neutral, so claims under this identity may arise from idiopathic neuralgia or from documented injury; (iii) evidence class - one six-case re-evaluation series and two management/assessment cohorts without incidence denominators or controlled comparison; (iv) the same cohorts document the neuropathic triad of burning pain, allodynia, and dysgeusia that is partly constitutive of the presentation.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-25: (i) no lingual-neuralgia-to-depressive-disorder edge - cognitive behaviour therapy was offered to 8 percent of the injury cohort and quality-of-life improvement was documented after surgery (PMID 22326447), but no condition-specific depression prevalence was quantified; reopening condition: a cohort or case-control quantifying depressive-disorder prevalence in lingual neuralgia or lingual nerve injury; (ii) no -> trigeminal-neuralgia or -> burning-mouth-syndrome edge (wrong-identity and direction guards; see todo); (iii) no -> taste-loss or ageusia edge (dysgeusia is a constitutive sensory symptom of the nerve injury rather than a downstream condition, and the located cohorts track it as a symptom); (iv) no -> sleep-apnea or -> dental edge (site siblings and airway pathways out of scope of the located evidence).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Chuang 2026 retrospective case series of treatment-refractory non-odontogenic orofacial pain documents six patients with objective negative dental findings and a median 17-month diagnostic delay whose re-evaluation under the International Classification of Orofacial Pain produced final diagnoses including lingual nerve injury, with pain intensity improving from a median numerical rating score of 8 to 0-2 after systematic diagnostic re-evaluation, and identifies premature single-cause attribution, overreliance on imaging or prior medication history, and insufficient neurologic examination as common pitfalls (PMID 42220291); the Renton and Yilmaz 2012 cohort of 216 iatrogenic trigeminal nerve injuries, 93 of them lingual nerve injuries, documents the chronic neuropathic pain management pathway - reassurance and counselling for 55 percent, medication for 5 percent, cognitive behaviour therapy for 8 percent, topical lidocaine patches reducing pain and allodynia, and exploratory surgery improving symptoms and reducing the neuropathic area in 18 lingual nerve injury patients (PMID 22326447); the Renton 2006 prospective series of 94 lingual nerve injuries after third molar surgery documents that conventional sensory tests were often unable to diagnose injury and were not predictive of outcome, with patient-reported subjective function identifying those at risk of permanent injury (PMID 16732250); the literature documents a reproducible chronic neuropathic tongue-pain presentation requiring an exclusionary dental, neurologic, and neuropathic workup without establishing that lingual neuralgia caused a distinct chronic pain disorder in any individual.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that lingual neuralgia caused an individual's chronic pain disorder: the neuropathic pain is the defining presentation of the neuralgia rather than a separate downstream condition, so the edge records presentation-and-workup matching; the evidence is a six-case re-evaluation series and two management cohorts dominated by iatrogenic injury after third molar surgery without incidence denominators, burning pain, allodynia, and dysgeusia are constitutive symptoms recorded in the same cohorts, and dental disease, temporomandibular disorders, trigeminal neuralgia, and burning mouth syndrome are competing explanations enumerated in the same literature - so no directional claim is made.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized nerve-injury sensitization route is described: lingual nerve trauma (most often iatrogenic, after third molar surgery) produces ectopic firing and central sensitization sustaining burning neuropathic tongue pain, allodynia, and dysgeusia, while repeated negative dental workups and delayed diagnosis amplify pain chronification and health care utilization; the located cohorts document the management pathway and the diagnostic-delay pattern, but the individual shares of injury severity, sensitization, and diagnostic odyssey remain hypotheses.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Chronic neuropathic tongue pain is documented in management and diagnostic re-evaluation cohorts of lingual nerve injury with documented exclusionary workups, but individual determination requires documented lingual neuralgia or lingual nerve injury with neurosensory findings (burning pain, allodynia, dysgeusia), a dated dental and neurologic exclusionary workup, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documentation of the lingual neuralgia diagnosis with etiology (idiopathic or iatrogenic, with any third molar or dental procedure records and dates), neurosensory findings (subjective pain distribution, allodynia, dysgeusia, with mechanosensory or trigeminal-evoked testing where performed) and their chronology; documentation of pain severity (numerical rating or visual analogue scores) and duration with dates; the exclusionary workup - dental examination with negative findings, imaging to exclude mandibular or tongue pathology, temporomandibular evaluation, and neurologic assessment distinguishing trigeminal neuralgia, burning mouth syndrome, and persistent idiopathic dentoalveolar pain; management history (reassurance, medications, topical lidocaine, cognitive behaviour therapy, exploratory surgery or neurectomy) with response; oral-surgery, orofacial-pain, or neurology assessment of the attribution
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Trigeminal neuralgia or another trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia
Burning mouth syndrome without identifiable nerve injury
Persistent idiopathic dentoalveolar pain or temporomandibular disorder
Dental or periapical disease missed on initial examination
Tongue-mucosal disease (candidiasis, glossitis, lichen planus, malignancy)
Central neuropathic pain or post-stroke tongue pain

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY as a case-matching pain edge on the genitofemoral-nerve-neuralgia and levator-ani-syndrome precedent: management and diagnostic-re-evaluation cohorts document a chronic neuropathic tongue-pain presentation with long diagnostic delay whose exclusionary dental, neurologic, and neuropathic workup mirrors the unexplained-chronic-pain evaluation, with documented improvement after the correct pathway (surgery, medication, or reassurance) was identified; because the pain is constitutive of the neuralgia, the cohorts are management-class without denominators, and competing orofacial diagnoses are enumerated in the same literature, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and records presentation-and-workup matching rather than a causal arrow.
